abstract: For positive geometric Syracuse letters, fixed-subcritical Fourier estimates do not quantify the loss as the mean drift approaches zero. We prove a uniform bound for $1/2\le p<\alpha=\log_3 2$: at primitive ternary conductor depth $n$, every power $n^{-A}$ has constant at most $\exp(C(A+1)^2\ell)$, where $\ell=\log(e/(\alpha-p))$. The argument combines an exact binomial renewal identity, a one-sided stopped-martingale exit estimate valid through criticality, and the previously established hierarchical packing mechanism. Optimizing the power gives $\exp[-c(\log n)^2/\ell]$ above an explicit onset, hence superpolynomial decay for every subpower approach to criticality. The nonnegative pair majorant obeys the same estimate, permitting matched-total conditioning with a square-root loss. We also prove a stopped version whose threshold retains the maximum of an exponential onset and an inverse-drift deficit term, yielding a quantitative allowance for omitted letters and bounded clock twists. A deterministic separated-triangle staircase, supported by cyclic conditioning and the same exact renewal identity, gives a matching abstract lower exponent. At criticality its no-white-epoch probability is at least $c_G n^{-3/2}$. Thus the subpower approach is necessary and sufficient for uniform superpolynomial decay over the abstract geometric class. The lower construction need not be an arithmetic black set and does not lower-bound complex Fourier coefficients. The proofs are analytic; a retained bounded rational audit checks finite identities only. No tilted joint-mixing or routing theorem, critical Fourier upper bound, or resolution of Collatz is claimed.

change_summary: Separate consolidated paper in response to the scope rejection of the proposed paper48/v3. Removes the unchanged untilted joint-mixing and routing material, cites accepted paper48/v2 as an input, explicitly states the inherited geometric profile theorem and its uniformity requirements, and keeps the near-critical upper bound, exact-total/stopped consequences and matching abstract lower construction together. Moves detailed drift bookkeeping to Appendix A, reintroduces every needed definition, renumbers references/equations, clarifies the renewal formula boundary and displacement notation, and provides a focused supplement with the unchanged finite audit. Scope remains primitive tilted Fourier/absolute-majorant estimates and abstract geometric sharpness, with no critical Fourier upper bound or arithmetic lower realization.

coauthors.contribution: Contributed the inherited hierarchical packing mechanism and independently audited the new uniform passage, white-exit, drift dependence, stopped estimates, and abstract sharpness construction and their integration.
